title: Line-Touch Dribble Shuttle
description: Players dribble out to each court line, touch it with the free hand while keeping the dribble low, and come back — a handling shuttle with a low-stance demand.

content.objective: Change direction and get low while keeping a protected dribble, with the touch-down forcing a real knee bend.
content.setup: Lines of three to four on the baseline, one ball per player in each line.
content.organization: First player in each line goes; the next starts when the previous one returns.
instructions: Dribble to the free-throw line extended, get low and touch it with the free hand, return to the baseline and touch it.
Dribble to the half-court line, touch, return and touch.
Dribble to the far free-throw line, touch, return.
Use the right hand going out and the left hand coming back.
Hand off to the next player in line.
coachingPoints: Bend the knees to touch, do not bend the back.
Keep the dribble on the outside of the body during the touch.
Change hands on the turn, not before it.
commonMistakes: Picking the ball up to touch the line.
Turning with the ball exposed in front of the body.
Rushing and losing the ball on the turn.
content.safety: Leave a full lane between lines; players stay in their own lane when turning.
progressions: Add a crossover at each line.
Race the lines against each other.
regressions: Use only the near half of the court.
Allow a two-hand catch at each line.
variations: Use the weak hand both ways.
Touch with the hand nearest the ball to force a protected turn.
successCriteria: Completes the shuttle without picking up the dribble.
Each touch made from a low stance.
content.gameApplication: Changing direction low and with the ball protected is how ball handlers turn away from pressure.
